ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.title: A Nurse for Another House
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.text: A child has been born in the rich house next door, and the mistress has no milk. They need a wet nurse, and their eye has fallen on your family: your mother {npc} is healthy and has milk to spare. The pay is generous - food, cloth, the household's goodwill. But is there enough milk for two?
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.go: Take the place, and feed you thin porridge at home
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.go.success: You were fed porridge from a spoon and put to the breast only in the evenings. You grew up thinner than the rich baby, but you held on to life with both fists - and for the first time in years your family ate their fill.
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.go.failure: Porridge was no substitute for milk: your belly ached and you cried with hunger at night. But at least there was food in the house.
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.both: Agree - but only if she can nurse you both
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.both.success: The mistress pulled a face but agreed. You and the rich baby were laid in one cradle, and {npc} nursed you both - you always first, as the story went later.
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.both.failure: The mistress would not hear of a stranger's baby in her house. {npc} stayed home with you - and seemed rather relieved.
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.stay: Refuse: her own child comes first
ev.k1_wet_nurse_job.stay.ok: The messenger was sent away empty-handed. The neighbours called it foolish, but you spent the winter asleep at a warm breast and regretted nothing.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.title: Harvest Days
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.text: Harvest has come: every pair of hands is needed in the fields, and your mother {npc} can't stay at home. And you can't even sit up yet. What is to be done with you all day?
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.field: Take you to the field and lay you in the shade at the edge
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.field.success: You spent the whole harvest lying in the shade of a tree, listening to the reapers call to one another. In the evenings {npc} found you either asleep or clutching a beetle in your fist.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.field.failure: The shade moved with the sun, and {npc} noticed too late. You overheated and burned with fever for two days.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.neighbor: Leave you with the old woman next door who no longer works the fields
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.neighbor.success: The old woman fed you from a spoon, sang with her toothless mouth and told you, a mere babe, her whole life story. You listened closely - she hadn't had a better listener in years.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.neighbor.failure: The old woman dozed off in the sun, and you rolled off your mat straight into the dust. A lump on your forehead, a graze on your cheek - and a howl the whole street could hear.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.alone: Swaddle you tight, leave you at home and run back to check
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.alone.success: You slept most of the day, and {npc} came running from the field at noon, soaked in sweat, fed you and ran back. The harvest was brought in on time.
ev.k1_harvest_cradle.alone.failure: When {npc} ran home at noon, you were hoarse from screaming and flies were crawling over your face. You were never left alone again.
ev.k1_guest_holds.title: The Guest Wants a Hold
ev.k1_guest_holds.text: A traveller has asked for a night's shelter, and now he is reaching out for you: he has six of his own, he says, he knows how. He is a kind, cheerful man - only he coughs so hard the lamp flame trembles.
ev.k1_guest_holds.let: Let him hold you: you don't refuse a guest
ev.k1_guest_holds.let.success: The guest rocked you like an old hand and whistled like a bird, and you laughed out loud for the first time. In the morning he left you a wooden bead for luck.
ev.k1_guest_holds.let.failure: The guest dandled you all evening, and three days later you started coughing too. The cough lasted until the new moon.
ev.k1_guest_holds.excuse: Say you're asleep and carry you off to a far corner
ev.k1_guest_holds.excuse.ok: The guest nodded as if he understood, but he was noticeably sadder all evening. Your family felt awkward; you didn't care.
ev.k1_guest_holds.wash: Let him - but first he must wash his hands and say a blessing over you
ev.k1_guest_holds.wash.success: The guest was surprised, but he washed and spoke an old blessing over you in his own tongue. His cough never caught you.
ev.k1_guest_holds.wash.failure: The guest took offence at all the ceremony, but held you anyway - and a few days later you were coughing all the same.
ev.k1_night_crying.title: Crying in the Night
ev.k1_night_crying.text: For three weeks now you have screamed every night - not from pain, not from hunger, you just scream as soon as it gets dark. The neighbours bang on the wall, and your mother {npc} falls asleep on her feet. The old women say night crying means something is troubling you.
ev.k1_night_crying.walk: Carry you in her arms until dawn, for as long as it takes
ev.k1_night_crying.walk.ok: For a month {npc} paced from corner to corner with you, humming the same tune. Then one night you simply fell asleep - and the crying stopped as suddenly as it had begun.
ev.k1_night_crying.draught: Give you a sleeping draught from the herb woman
ev.k1_night_crying.draught.success: The draught smelled bitter, but you fell asleep the very first night and slept until morning. The whole house woke up rested for the first time in a month.
ev.k1_night_crying.draught.failure: You slept for nearly a whole day and night, and {npc} was more frightened than by all the screaming put together. The draught was poured away, and the herb woman was never called again.
ev.k1_night_crying.rite: Call the old woman who whispers charms, to drive off whatever troubles you
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.christian: Ask the priest to sprinkle the cradle with holy water
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.islamic: Recite the protective suras over the cradle
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.jewish: Hang an amulet against Lilith over the cradle
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.dharmic: Tie a blessed thread round your wrist against evil spirits
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.east_asian: Paste a note at the crossroads - "A child cries at night" - so passers-by read it and carry the trouble away
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.polytheist: Put a charm under the cradle and make an offering to the household gods
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.mesoamerican: Smoke the cradle with copal and ask the gods to drive off the night spirits
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.andean: Call the healer to call back your frightened soul
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.african: Ask the diviner which of the ancestors is troubling you
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.success: Whether it was that or you simply grew out of it - three nights later the house was quiet.
ev.k1_night_crying.rite.failure: Everything was done by the book. You sat through the whole rite perfectly calm - and started screaming the moment the lamp went out.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.title: The Lost Charm
ev.k1_lost_amulet.text: The charm that has hung round your neck since your first days is gone: the cord wore through, and you can't say where you dropped it - you can barely talk. Your mother {npc} goes pale: a baby without a charm, people say, is like a house without a door.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.text.christian: The little cross put on you at your baptism is gone: the cord wore through, and you can't say where you dropped it - you can barely talk. Your mother {npc} goes pale: a baby without a cross, people say, has no protection.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.search: Turn the whole house and yard upside down
ev.k1_lost_amulet.search.success: The charm turned up by evening - in your own bedding, where you had hidden it yourself. Everyone breathed again, and the new cord was braided three times as strong.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.search.failure: They searched for three days, shook out every mat and every pot - nothing. In the end they had to let it go.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new: Have a new one made by someone who knows how
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.christian: Buy a new little cross and have it blessed in church
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.islamic: Order a new pouch with a verse of the Qur'an
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.jewish: Order a new amulet with the holy names
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.dharmic: Bring a new blessed thread from the temple
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.east_asian: Get a new paper charm from the temple
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.polytheist: Buy a new amulet and dedicate it to the gods
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.mesoamerican: Tie a new thread with a jade bead on you
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.andean: Braid a new llama-wool cord and have the healer speak over it
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.african: Order a new leather charm from the healer
ev.k1_lost_amulet.new.ok: The new charm didn't come cheap, but {npc} slept soundly again. The old one stayed hidden somewhere in the house, biding its time.
ev.k1_lost_amulet.shrug: Decide it's people, not strings, that will keep you safe
ev.k1_lost_amulet.shrug.ok: The neighbours gasped, but {npc} only held you closer. You grew up without a charm - and grow you did.
ev.k1_first_haircut.title: First Hair
ev.k1_first_haircut.text: It's time for your first haircut. That's no small matter: a baby's first hair, people say, holds its fate, and your mother {npc} has spent a week deciding how to cut it and what to do with it.
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite: Do it all by custom, with guests and a feast
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.christian: Call the priest to snip your hair crosswise and say a prayer
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.islamic: Shave your head and give alms for your health
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.jewish: Hold the first haircut with a feast and a blessing
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.dharmic: Take you to the temple and shave your head as vowed
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.east_asian: Shave your head but leave a tuft on top, and offer a lock to the ancestors
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.polytheist: Dedicate your first hair to the gods and leave it at the shrine
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.mesoamerican: Cut your hair on a lucky day chosen by the priest
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.andean: Hold a rutuchikuy: every guest cuts a lock and leaves a gift
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.african: Give your first hair to an elder to bury by the sacred tree
ev.k1_first_haircut.rite.ok: The guests ate, sang and praised you over one another, while you sat with an oddly bare head, feeling it with both hands.
ev.k1_first_haircut.home: Cut it quietly at home and keep one lock
ev.k1_first_haircut.home.ok: {npc} cut your hair herself while you slept, tied one soft lock with a thread and tucked it away. Where, nobody saw.
ev.k1_first_haircut.wait: Don't cut it at all: let it grow until you're stronger
ev.k1_first_haircut.wait.success: Your curls grew to your shoulders, and strangers couldn't tell whether you were a boy or a girl. You were very pleased with yourself.
ev.k1_first_haircut.wait.failure: Lice moved into your long mop, and you had to be shaved anyway - this time with no ceremony at all.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.title: The Cradle
ev.k1_cradle_hang.text: Your father {npc} spent three evenings making you a cradle - with a carved headboard and a good deal of extra effort. Now the whole family is arguing about where to put it.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.beam: Hang it from the roof beam so it can swing
ev.k1_cradle_hang.beam.success: The cradle swung at a single push, and you fell asleep to its creak faster than to any song. {npc} walked about as proud as if he had built a palace.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.beam.failure: A month later the rope wore through and the cradle crashed to the floor with you in it. Everyone was frightened except you: you didn't even wake up.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.hearth: Set it by the hearth, where it's warmest
ev.k1_cradle_hang.hearth.success: By the hearth it was warm and smelled of smoke and supper. You grew up watching the fire, and loved it all your life.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.hearth.failure: One day an ember shot out of the hearth right onto your blanket. The spark was slapped out by hand, but you kept a little mark on your cheek as a souvenir.
ev.k1_cradle_hang.together: Who needs a cradle - you'll sleep with everyone in the family bed
ev.k1_cradle_hang.together.ok: You slept in a warm heap of family and never knew what it was to be alone. The carved cradle ended up holding grain - and {npc} sulked about it for a long time.
ev.k1_weaning.title: Time to Wean
ev.k1_weaning.text: You are running about with a mouth full of teeth, and still you won't give up the breast. Your mother {npc} has grown thin, and the neighbours all say the same thing: it's time to wean.
ev.k1_weaning.bitter: Smear the breast with a bitter herb and be done with it
ev.k1_weaning.bitter.success: You latched on, made a face, howled in outrage - and never asked again. A week later you were wolfing down porridge with both cheeks full.
ev.k1_weaning.bitter.failure: You sobbed for three days and ate almost nothing. You were weaned all right, but you grew thin and kept reaching for your mother at night for a long time.
ev.k1_weaning.slowly: Wean you bit by bit: first in the day, then at night
ev.k1_weaning.slowly.ok: It took two months and a great deal of patience. You barely noticed when you stopped asking for the breast - but you remembered being distracted with songs.
ev.k1_weaning.keep: Nurse you for as long as you want: milk beats any porridge
ev.k1_weaning.keep.ok: You nursed until you were nearly three, and the neighbours shook their heads. But you fell ill noticeably less often than the children next door.
ev.k1_sibling_guard.title: Jealousy
ev.k1_sibling_guard.text: Your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} is jealous: since you arrived, nobody looks at {g=npc_sex:him|her} any more. Yesterday {g=npc_sex:he|she} "accidentally" rocked the cradle so hard you nearly flew out onto the floor.
ev.k1_sibling_guard.guard: Give {g=npc_sex:him|her} an important job: guarding you
ev.k1_sibling_guard.guard.success: {npc} took the job seriously: shooed away flies, dogs and neighbours and let no one touch you without asking. The jealousy vanished without a trace - now you were {g=npc_sex:his|her} property.
ev.k1_sibling_guard.guard.failure: As a guard {g=npc_sex:he|she} was hopeless: within an hour {npc} had run off to play, leaving you in the care of the flies.
ev.k1_sibling_guard.scold.ok: {npc} sulked in the corner until evening and never came near the cradle again - not to hurt you, and not to play either.
ev.k1_sibling_guard.time: Give {g=npc_sex:him|her} more attention and leave you in the cradle more
ev.k1_sibling_guard.time.ok: {npc} thawed within a week and even began showing you {g=npc_sex:his|her} treasures - pebbles and feathers. You lay in the cradle and waited patiently for your turn to be noticed.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.title: A Stuffy Nose
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.text: Your nose is blocked: you can't nurse and breathe at the same time, so you let go of the breast and scream with hunger and outrage. Your mother {npc} has already tried everything she knows.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.suck: Suck your nose clear, the way grandmothers always have
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.suck.success: The method was old, unlovely and reliable. You sneezed, took a deep breath and latched on greedily at once.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.suck.failure: Your nose was cleared ten times a day, but the cold went down to your chest, and for a week you wheezed like an old dog.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.steam.success: The steam smelled of herbs and honey. You scrunched up your face and sneezed, but by evening you were breathing through your nose.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.steam.failure: The steam was too hot: you turned bright red and screamed louder than ever, and your nose stayed as blocked as before.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.oil: Dab your nostrils with oil and prop your head up
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.oil.success: You were laid on a folded garment with your head raised, and by morning the cold had let go.
ev.k1_stuffy_nose.oil.failure: The oil didn't help, but you got it all over yourself, right up to the ears. The cold went away on its own - a week later.
ev.k1_colic.title: Colic
ev.k1_colic.text: Every evening, as if by arrangement, the cramps come: you pull your knees to your belly, turn purple and scream for hours. The neighbour swears it's just your tummy and will pass by the third month. But the third month is still a long way off - for you and for everyone at home.
ev.k1_colic.warm: Warm your belly with a hot cloth and carry you face-down along her arm
ev.k1_colic.warm.success: {npc} learned to carry you along her arm like a kitten on a branch, and you went quiet almost at once. By the third month it really had passed.
ev.k1_colic.warm.failure: Nothing worked. You screamed every evening right up to the third month - just as the neighbour had promised.
ev.k1_colic.seeds: Give you water steeped with fragrant seeds
ev.k1_colic.seeds.success: The water smelled sweet and spicy. You drank it from a spoon, hiccupped loudly - and fell asleep.
ev.k1_colic.seeds.failure: You spat the infusion out with such disgust that {npc} finally gave up. The colic passed on its own when its time came.
ev.k1_colic.healer: Call the wise woman to "set" your tummy right
ev.k1_colic.healer.success: The wise woman kneaded your belly, whispered, blew on it - and suddenly you broke wind loudly and fell asleep with a blissful smile. She took her fee and left with the air of a conqueror.
ev.k1_colic.healer.failure: The wise woman kneaded so hard that you screamed even louder than before. It passed on its own in the end - just as the neighbour had promised.
ev.k1_house_snake.title: A Snake by the Cradle
ev.k1_house_snake.text: Your mother {npc} came back with the water and froze in the doorway: by your cradle, coiled in a patch of sunlight, lies a snake. You are cooing and reaching out for it. The old folk say every house has its guardian snake, and it must never be harmed.
ev.k1_house_snake.leave: Leave it be: it's the guardian of the house
ev.k1_house_snake.leave.success: The snake lay there, warmed itself and slid away under the threshold. It was seen many times after - always near you, and it never harmed anyone. The family decided you had a special guardian.
ev.k1_house_snake.leave.failure: The snake slid away, but {npc} had such a fright that her milk dried up for a week. You were fed porridge and pitied.
ev.k1_house_snake.carry: Carefully carry it far from the house on a stick
ev.k1_house_snake.carry.success: The snake hung over the stick like a rope and didn't struggle. It was carried beyond the fence and let go with a bow - just in case.
ev.k1_house_snake.carry.failure: The snake twisted, slipped off the stick and vanished into a crack under the wall. Now everyone knows it's somewhere in the house, and nobody sleeps easy.
ev.k1_house_snake.kill.ok: The snake was killed with a hoe. The neighbours shook their heads: killing a house snake brings bad luck. No bad luck came, but the gossip lasted a year.
ev.k1_cold_bath.title: Toughening Up
ev.k1_cold_bath.text: The old man next door, who raised nine, has advice: dunk a baby in cold water every morning and it will grow up as tough as stone. Those who don't listen to him, he says, raise weaklings.
ev.k1_cold_bath.cold: Dunk you in cold water every morning
ev.k1_cold_bath.cold.success: You shrieked so loudly the whole street could hear, then turned as red as a berry and slept like a log. Illness seemed to pass you by.
ev.k1_cold_bath.cold.failure: After the third dunking you began to cough, and a week later you were burning with fever. The baths were stopped, and nobody listened to the neighbour again.
ev.k1_cold_bath.warm: Bathe you in warm water by the hearth, as always
ev.k1_cold_bath.warm.ok: The neighbour grumbled that you'd grow up soft. You splashed about in the warm water and had no idea.
ev.k1_cold_bath.rarely: Bathe you less often: water, people say, is where illness comes from
ev.k1_cold_bath.rarely.ok: You were wiped with a damp cloth and rubbed with fat, but nobody hurried to wash you all over. To be honest, you did not smell of roses.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.title: The Loom and the Cradle
ev.k1_loom_rocking.text: Your mother {npc} has to finish a length of cloth before the festival - she has been promised payment for it. But the moment she sits at the loom, you start to scream.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.foot: Tie the cradle rope to her foot and rock you without stopping work
ev.k1_loom_rocking.foot.success: Her foot rocked, her hands wove, her lips sang. The cloth was ready on time, and you got so used to falling asleep to the clack of the loom that you couldn't sleep without it.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.foot.failure: The thread tangled, the cradle jerked, you screamed. The cloth wasn't ready in time, and the pay was cut.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.soother: Give you a rag with chewed porridge in it to suck
ev.k1_loom_rocking.soother.success: You sucked the rag so earnestly that you forgot to scream. The cloth was finished on time.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.soother.failure: The rag was sweet but not very clean. Two days later your belly ached, and the work stopped anyway.
ev.k1_loom_rocking.girl: Get the neighbours' girl to mind you for a bowl of stew
ev.k1_loom_rocking.girl.ok: The girl was about seven and minded you like a doll: dressed you up, rocked you, fed you pretend meals. You were delighted.
ev.k1_borrow_luck.title: A Neighbour's Grief
ev.k1_borrow_luck.text: A neighbour has come with a bow: two of her babies did not live to see a year, and now a third has been born. She asks for one of your old swaddling cloths - a healthy child's things, people say, ward off misfortune. Your mother {npc} hesitates: what if your luck goes out the door with the cloth?
ev.k1_borrow_luck.give: Give her the cloth - and a second one too
ev.k1_borrow_luck.give.ok: The neighbour burst into tears and left, clutching the cloths to her chest. Your luck didn't seem any the less for it.
ev.k1_borrow_luck.refuse: Refuse: you don't give your luck away
ev.k1_borrow_luck.refuse.ok: The neighbour left without a word. From then on she greeted your household only every other time.
ev.k1_borrow_luck.scrap: Give her not the cloth but a scrap of it: there's luck enough for two
ev.k1_borrow_luck.scrap.success: The neighbour sewed the scrap into her baby's clothes. And by every sign, you were none the poorer in luck.
ev.k1_borrow_luck.scrap.failure: The neighbour took the scrap but was hurt: begrudged her a whole cloth, she said. Things stayed strained between the houses.
ev.k1_old_ways.title: The Old Ways
ev.k1_old_ways.text: Grandmother, who raised half a dozen children, insists on the old ways: swaddle tight, no bathing and no showing you to anyone until the proper time has passed, and a rub with salt and oil at night. Your mother {npc} would rather do things her own way - but in this house, nobody argues with Grandmother.
ev.k1_old_ways.old.success: Grandmother ran the house like a general. You lay there, a tightly wrapped bundle, and grew up remarkably placid - and Grandmother took all the credit.
ev.k1_old_ways.old.failure: The salt made your skin red and cracked. Grandmother said that was how it should be, but the salt was quietly put away.
ev.k1_old_ways.mother: Raise you the way your mother sees fit
ev.k1_old_ways.mother.ok: Grandmother took offence and spoke to no one for a week. Then she came, picked you up - and explained, all the same, the proper way to rock you.
ev.k1_old_ways.half: Swaddle Grandmother's way, and do the rest their own way
ev.k1_old_ways.half.success: Peace in the house was kept, and you didn't seem to notice a thing.
ev.k1_old_ways.half.failure: Neither was satisfied, and each secretly redid whatever the other had done. You were swaddled and unswaddled three times a day.
ev.k1_mother_dream.title: A Bad Dream
ev.k1_mother_dream.text: Your mother {npc} woke in the night in a cold sweat: she had dreamed the river was carrying you away. The dream was so vivid that she held you in her arms until morning.
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner: Go to an interpreter of dreams
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.christian: Go to the holy elder to have the dream explained
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.islamic: Ask a learned interpreter of dreams
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.jewish: Ask a sage what such a dream means
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.dharmic: Ask the priest and have your horoscope cast
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.east_asian: Go to a fortune-teller to have the dream read
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.polytheist: Go to the seer at the shrine
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.mesoamerican: Go to the priest who reads fate in the sacred calendar
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.andean: Ask the healer to read the coca leaves
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.african: Go to the diviner and have the shells cast
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.success: The interpreter listened and smiled: a river in a dream means a long life - only it will carry you far from home. {npc} was comforted - and thoughtful.
ev.k1_mother_dream.diviner.failure: The interpreter was silent for a long time, then said you must not be taken near water for three months. {npc} obeyed - and flinched at every splash.
ev.k1_mother_dream.away: Move the cradle away from the door and keep you away from the river
ev.k1_mother_dream.away.ok: The cradle was moved to the farthest corner, and {npc} went down to the river alone, glancing back over her shoulder. The dream never came again.
ev.k1_mother_dream.nothing: Tell herself it was only a dream
ev.k1_mother_dream.nothing.ok: By morning the dream was lost in the day's chores. And you, as luck would have it, grew up loving water more than anything in the world.
ev.k1_left_hand.title: The Left Hand
ev.k1_left_hand.text: A spoon, a pebble, someone else's bead - you grab everything with your left hand. The neighbours whisper: the left hand is unlucky, and a left-hander's life will turn out crooked. Someone advises tying it to your side before it's too late.
ev.k1_left_hand.tie: Tie up your left hand so you learn to use the right
ev.k1_left_hand.tie.success: You raged and cried, but a month later you were reaching for your spoon with your right. Only stones you kept throwing with the left.
ev.k1_left_hand.tie.failure: Your hand was kept tied for a month, and you screamed the whole month. The moment it was untied, you grabbed the spoon with your left. After that they left you alone.
ev.k1_left_hand.let: Leave it be: whichever hand grabs, let it hold
ev.k1_left_hand.let.ok: So you stayed left-handed. The neighbours pursed their lips, while you ate, drew in the dust and threw stones with your left hand - and hit what you aimed at.
ev.k1_first_shirt.title: First Clothes
ev.k1_first_shirt.text: It's time to sew your first clothes. The old folk say a baby's first little shirt should be made from the father's worn clothes - so the father's strength passes to the child. But your father {npc} is in patched clothes himself.
ev.k1_first_shirt.father: Sew it from his old clothes, as custom says
ev.k1_first_shirt.father.ok: {npc} gave up his last old shirt and went about as proud as if he had given you a whole house.
ev.k1_first_shirt.new: Buy new cloth: let you have something of your own
ev.k1_first_shirt.new.ok: The cloth was brand new, stiff and smelled of the dye-works. The neighbours fingered it enviously, while you sat in it and itched.
ev.k1_first_shirt.neighbor: Take hand-me-downs from neighbours whose children grew up healthy
ev.k1_first_shirt.neighbor.ok: You were the fifth to wear it, and it was all patches - but a lucky garment, people said: everyone who wore it grew up.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.title: Earrings
ev.k1_ear_piercing.text: It's time to pierce your ears - where you live, every girl has it done, and the sooner, the fewer the tears. Your mother {npc} already has the needle and thread ready.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.now: Pierce them now, before you're old enough to remember the pain
ev.k1_ear_piercing.now.success: You squealed, took offence at the whole world - and forgot about it a minute later. Threads stayed in your ears, and then your first earrings.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.now.failure: One ear festered and swelled. It was salved and washed, and in two weeks it healed - a little crooked.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.healer: Call the old woman who knows how: she has a light hand
ev.k1_ear_piercing.healer.success: The old woman muttered something, distracted you with a shiny bead - and it was all over before you had time to cry.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.healer.failure: Even a light hand has its heavy days: your ear swelled up, and for a week you wouldn't let anyone touch it.
ev.k1_ear_piercing.later.ok: They decided to wait. The neighbours wondered aloud: whoever heard of a girl with bare ears?
ev.k1_milk_kin.title: Milk Kin
ev.k1_milk_kin.text: A richly dressed stranger studied you for a long time, then asked whether you were the one who had been nursed at the same breast as them. It was the very child from the rich house for whom a wet nurse had once been found. Milk kinship, people say, can be stronger than blood.
ev.k1_milk_kin.patron: Ask them to put in a good word for you
ev.k1_milk_kin.patron.ok: They promised to help - and, to your surprise, kept their word. The right doors began to open a little more easily.
ev.k1_milk_kin.friend: Just sit and talk about the things neither of you remembers
ev.k1_milk_kin.friend.ok: You talked until dark, and by the end it no longer mattered which of you was rich. Since then you meet whenever you can.
ev.k1_milk_kin.pass: Bow and walk on: the favour of the rich is slippery ground
ev.k1_milk_kin.pass.ok: You walked away without looking back and felt oddly proud all day.
ev.k1_left_hand_later.title: The Wrong Hand
ev.k1_left_hand_later.text: The one teaching you your trade winces every time you pick up a tool with your left hand: "That's not how it's done. Learn the proper way while you still can."
ev.k1_left_hand_later.switch: Switch to your right hand, as you're told
ev.k1_left_hand_later.switch.ok: For a long time your right hand felt foreign and clumsy. But you stubbornly kept at it until you no longer noticed the difference.
ev.k1_left_hand_later.keep: Keep working left-handed and prove you're just as good
ev.k1_left_hand_later.keep.success: You showed that your left hand worked as well as anyone's, and in some things better. Your teacher grunted and let it go.
ev.k1_left_hand_later.keep.failure: Your teacher didn't argue - he simply stopped calling you for real work. You had to figure out a great deal on your own.
ev.k1_amulet_found.text: When the old hearth was being rebuilt, a tiny bundle fell out of a crack - the very charm that went missing when you were a baby. The whole house laughed: all those years it had been watching over you from inside the wall.
ev.k1_amulet_found.text.christian: When the old hearth was being rebuilt, a tiny cross on a rotted cord fell out of a crack - the very one that went missing when you were a baby. The whole house laughed: all those years it had been watching over you from inside the wall.
ev.k1_hair_lock.text: Your mother {npc} took a little bundle from its hiding place, and inside was a soft baby curl tied with a thread. "Yours," she said. "The very first." You never knew she had kept it all these years.
ev.k1_sibling_defends.text: The neighbourhood boys snatched your toy - and out of nowhere {npc} came flying at them. "Hands off! That's mine!" {g=npc_sex:he|she} yelled, just as {g=npc_sex:he|she} once had over your cradle, and the boys scattered like leaves in the wind.
ev.k1_hardy.text: While the whole household is laid up with colds, you alone are on your feet - as usual. The neighbours still remember how you were dunked in cold water as a baby, and hold you up as an example: that's what toughening up does.
ev.k1_neighbor_kid.text: The neighbours' child who was once given your swaddling cloth grew up alive, healthy and noisy. In that house they still call you "our good-luck charm", and the two of you have been firm friends ever since.
ev.k1_m_mother_smell.text: You couldn't tell faces apart yet, but you knew one smell better than anything in the world: hearth smoke, milk and warm skin. That was how your mother {npc} smelled - and in the dark you knew her before she said a word.
ev.k1_m_rain_roof.text: In the night the rain came and drummed on the roof. You lay awake listening as it eased off and picked up again - and fell asleep without noticing when.
ev.k1_m_first_laugh.text: The old man from next door sneezed so loudly that dust rained down from the shelf - and for the first time you laughed out loud. He sneezed on purpose all evening, and you kept on laughing.
ev.k1_m_own_feet.text: You discovered that you had feet, and it was the great discovery of the year. You grabbed them, pulled them into your mouth and were most surprised when they wiggled on their own.
ev.k1_m_hen_cradle.text: A hen took a fancy to your cradle while you slept and laid an egg in it, right beside you. Your first treasure was promptly taken away and boiled.
ev.k1_m_firelight.text: In the evenings you watched the fire for ages: shadows leapt across the walls, and one of the grown-ups made a dog or a bird with their fingers. You grabbed at the shadows and got cross that they wouldn't be caught.
ev.k1_m_hiccups.text: You got the hiccups - small, stubborn ones that lasted half a day. Everyone in the house had a sure cure: you were given water, startled, tickled and had a thread stuck to your forehead. The hiccups went away on their own, but everyone was sure it was their cure that worked.
ev.k1_m_first_sun.text: You were carried outside into the bright light for the first time. You screwed up your eyes and sneezed at the sun - and everyone around laughed as if you had done something very clever.
ev.k1_m_morning_bird.text: Every morning the same bird landed on the roof and struck up its song. You woke before everyone else and lay with your head turned towards the sound - waiting for it, it seemed, like a guest.
ev.k1_m_beard.text: You grabbed a guest by the beard and wouldn't let go, no matter how they coaxed you. The guest groaned, your family blushed, and you beamed: you'd never had such a splendid toy.
ev.k1_m_who_resembles.text: You were passed from hand to hand, and everyone found something of their own: you had Grandfather's nose, Grandmother's ears, and the temper of your great-grandfather - yes, that one. They argued about you all evening while you slept peacefully in someone's lap.
ev.k1_m_asleep_together.text: Your mother {npc} was nursing you in the half-dark and fell asleep herself in the middle of a lullaby. And so you both slept until morning - you on her breast, she leaning against the wall - and no one in the house dared wake you.
ev.k1_m_puddle.text: After the rain you found a puddle and sat right down in it. You slapped the water with your palms, splashes flew everywhere, and it was, beyond all doubt, the best day of your life.
ev.k1_m_leaves.text: You were laid in the shade of a tree, and for a long time you watched the leaves stirring above you: light, shadow, light, shadow. You reached up to them and told them something in your own language.
ev.k1_m_stranger_fear.text: Only yesterday you reached out to anyone at all, and today you suddenly burst into tears the moment a strange face leaned over you. Now you know exactly who belongs here and who doesn't.
ev.k1_m_bite.text: You were nursing - and suddenly decided to try out your new teeth. Your mother {npc} yelped so loudly the neighbours came running, and you laughed: what a funny noise!
ev.k1_m_moon_reach.text: On a warm night you were carried outside, and for the first time you saw the moon - big, round and very close. You reached for it and howled with indignation that nobody would hand it to you.
ev.k1_m_father_hum.text: Your father {npc} didn't know any lullabies, so whenever he was left with you, he would murmur everything that came to mind: the neighbours, the relatives, all the jobs to finish before harvest. You fell asleep to that list faster than to any song.
ev.k1_m_own_name.text: Someone called your name - and you turned round. For the first time. You had been called that since the day you were born, but only now did you understand that the word meant you.
ev.k1_m_hen_cradle.text.MAY: A turkey hen took to wandering into the house and settling down by your cradle. She looked at you with one eye, you looked at her with two, and both of you were very pleased.
ev.k1_m_hen_cradle.text.AMR: A turkey hen took to wandering into the house and settling down by your cradle. She looked at you with one eye, you looked at her with two, and both of you were very pleased.
ev.k1_m_hen_cradle.text.cusco: Guinea pigs scurried squeaking across the floor of the house, and you watched them from your cradle for hours. Once one even crept under your blanket to get warm.
ev.k1_m_hen_cradle.text.quito: Guinea pigs scurried squeaking across the floor of the house, and you watched them from your cradle for hours. Once one even crept under your blanket to get warm.
ev.k1_m_beard.text.JPN: You grabbed a guest by the topknot and wouldn't let go, no matter how they coaxed you. The guest groaned, your family bowed and blushed, and you beamed: you'd never had such a splendid toy.
ev.k1_m_beard.text.MAY: You grabbed a guest by his heavy ear ornament and wouldn't let go, no matter how they coaxed you. The guest groaned, your family blushed, and you beamed: you'd never had such a splendid toy.
ev.k1_m_beard.text.AMR: You grabbed a guest by his heavy ear ornament and wouldn't let go, no matter how they coaxed you. The guest groaned, your family blushed, and you beamed: you'd never had such a splendid toy.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text: You were taken to a shrine for the first time: half-darkness, the smell of incense, someone's quiet voice. You didn't cry - you just stared wide-eyed at the little flames.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.christian: You were taken to church for the first time: half-darkness, flickering candles, the smell of incense and singing from somewhere above. You didn't cry - you just stared wide-eyed at the little flames.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.islamic: You were carried to the mosque for the first time. The muezzin's voice floated out over the rooftops, and you went still in someone's arms, turning your head towards the sound as if you knew it.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.jewish: You were taken to the synagogue for the first time. The men prayed in a sing-song, swaying, and you swayed along with them in someone's arms.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.dharmic: You were taken to the temple for the first time: the ringing of bells, the scent of flowers and ghee, the little flames of the lamps. You didn't cry - you just stared wide-eyed.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.east_asian: You were held up to the ancestral altar for the first time and shown to the name tablets: here, this is one more of us. The incense smoke tickled your nose, you sneezed - and everyone agreed the ancestors were pleased.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.polytheist: You were taken to the shrine for the first time and presented to the gods: smoke over the altar, statues in the half-dark, the priest's quiet words. You didn't cry - you just stared wide-eyed.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.mesoamerican: You were taken to the temple for the first time: blue copal smoke, the boom of conch trumpets, the painted faces of the priests. You didn't cry - you just stared wide-eyed.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.andean: You were carried to the huaca for the first time - the sacred stone on the hill. The grown-ups laid coca leaves before it and whispered your name, so the place would remember you.
ev.k1_m_first_shrine.text.african: You were taken to the ancestors' shrine for the first time. An elder poured water on the ground and spoke your name - so the departed would know the family had grown.
